messages:
Liz: quick sketch for a follow-up RFC: "regional ramp-and-hold" policy to avoid global swapbacks when only a region is flapping. dropping the sketch here for feedback. https://redwood.example.com/rfc/123

Omar: nice. how do we choose "hold" thresholds? per-tenant p95 + sudden error spike? @liz

Jun: i'd use two signals: latency p95 and error-rate. policy fires when both exceed thresholds for N seconds, then ramp a percentage away and enter a hold window.

Anya: session affinity concern: aggressive swapbacks break long chats. we need a graceful path for in-flight sessions.

Liz: plan: session-tagged affinity + sticky grace window. existing sessions remain on original variant up to 30m; new sessions go to fallback. avoids context loss.

Omar: exposing policies as declarative YAML would help Console/runtime share the contract and make audits easier.

Liz: agreed. compact policy spec idea below:

```yaml
policy_name: regional_ramp_and_hold
scopes: [region]
regions: [us-west-2, eu-central-1]
signals:
  - name: latency_p95
    threshold_ms: 350
  - name: error_rate
    threshold_pct: 1.5
window_secs: 60
actions:
  - type: ramp_down
    amount_pct: 50
  - type: hold
    hold_minutes: 10
session_grace_minutes: 30
backoff_strategy: exponential
semantic_regression:
  delta_pct: 2.0
  probe_eval_hook: true
```

Jun: nit: prefer `semantic_regression` not `quality_gate`. also require a probe-eval hook: run a small eval during hold and auto-failback if drift > delta.

Anya: can Optimize automatically schedule that eval and surface results in Console?

Liz: yes. `hold` lifecycle will trigger Optimize eval jobs. failing evals auto-route to fallback until manual review.

Omar: runtime detail: KV/prefix cache reconciliation. if sessions stick to old variant we risk stale cache when shifting traffic later.

Liz: options in runbook: warm caches on fallback before ramp, use short TTLs for session keys during rollouts, or dual-write at the adapter layer for a reconciliation window. each has cost/complexity tradeoffs; i'll enumerate them in RFC.

Jun: include a manual override flag that forces global swapback for severe incidents and emits an audit trail.

oncall-bot: deploy-check: no canary-sim attached. run `./tools/canary-sim --policy regional_ramp_and_hold` and paste results before merge. :robot_face:

Omar: i'll run the sim and post results later. one more: how do pinned tenants behave?

Liz: by default pinned tenants bypass automatic fallback (enterprise SLA). add a tenant-level override to opt into auto-fallback.

Anya: add Console metrics: per-region p95, error_rate, active_holds, session_affected_count, eval_drift_pct. make them first-class.

Liz: will update RFC with YAML, runbook checklist, cache options, and sim notes. thanks all :thumbsup:

Omar: posting sim after lunch.

Jun: looks good. label as rfc/experiment-fallback and i'll review tomorrow.
